claims.feature: Forgotten Realms terms in the general guide
claims.claim: The general guide carries a short Realms list: Goodman/Goodwoman capped, 'goodsir' lowercased, 'godsforsaken' as the Realms form of godforsaken, and 'the Realms' only after 'the Forgotten Realms'.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')
claims.quote: goodsir (a form of address, not capped)

claims.claim: 'Godsforsaken' is the established Realms form but is not required in other polytheistic settings, since 'godforsaken' has no necessary monotheistic sense.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')

claims.claim: 'Fellowship' is avoided for a party because of its Tolkien association and because D&D parties are often fractious or mercenary; 'party', 'group', 'band', or 'company' are preferred.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')

claims.claim: Standard abbreviations are fixed (PH, DMG, MM, gp, d100, AC, DC, DM, XP, HD, hp, NPC).
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')

claims.claim: The superseded 2013 guide banned singular they outside informal contexts like dialogue.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.04a (2013)
claims.quote: Don’t use “they” or “their” as singular pronouns

claims.claim: The 2013 guide framed gender neutrality as assuming a readership of both men and women, a framing dropped in 2019 for 'we don't assume a gender identity'.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.04a (2013)
claims.quote: readership includes both men and women

claims.claim: Sections absent from v1.04a and present in v1.08a include Gender-Specific Suffixes, Headings, Sidebars, Bulleted Lists, Appendix References, and Adventuring Parties (verified by heading presence in both texts).
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.04a (2013)

claims.feature: existence of a post-2019 house style guide
claims.claim: A Word version of the house style guide, authored by Kim Mohan and last modified by Judy Bauer on 2021-07-06 at Wizards of the Coast, ships inside the Dungeoncraft Pack (2023-12-04) and postdates the public v1.08a PDF.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: The 2021 docx cites merriam-webster.com rather than the printed 11th edition Collegiate.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: The 2021 docx reverses the 2019 rule: 'man' and 'woman' may now describe the gender of any people, so 'dwarf man' and 'gnome woman' are fine.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: we can write “dwarf man” or “gnome woman.”

claims.claim: The 2021 docx allows they/their/them/themself for a person of unknown gender without the 2019 'don't abuse this liberty' caveat, requiring only a clear antecedent.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: you must ensure that the pronoun’s antecedent is clear

claims.claim: In running text a person's preferred pronoun (he, she, or they) is used; in rules text 'it' is used.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: Descriptive text uses they/them for Humanoids and other sapient creatures of unknown gender (including vampires), and 'it' for animals, cosmic horrors, and extraplanar creatures.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: A beholder never keeps its promises.

claims.claim: Where 'they' would be ambiguous the sentence is reworded to avoid pronouns, e.g. by switching to the plural.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.feature: 'it' for dehumanizing effect is an exception
claims.claim: Using 'it' for a sapient monster to emphasize inhumanity is allowed only as a rare deliberate effect.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
